annotations.text:
WHERE A PRINTER LIVES ON THE WALL -- THE QUESTION

The brain can now find and follow 3D printers (docs/printers.md, branch printers): what each one is doing, in its own words, with its camera, its temperatures and a short list of things a wall may do -- pause, resume, stop, cool down, switch spools, later, help. Nothing on the wall or the phone shows any of it, and per section 1 nothing will until a board is chosen.

THE HOUSE HAS THREE. Atlas is printing a phone stand, 42%, layer 118 of 280, done at 4:20 PM, in white PLA, nozzle 220, bed 60, chamber 38. Juno stopped with a toolhead that is not answering. Vega is ready with no spools loaded. Every board uses those values, and every sentence a printer says is the printer's own.

WHAT IS CONTESTED is where a printer lives, and the three directions are three whole answers: in its room, as a thing among things (A); on the time-of-day tab for as long as there is a print, the way a show that is playing leads it (B); on Cameras, as the camera on it with its words laid over the frame (C). How progress, the camera and attention show follows from where it lives, so each board answers those too.

WHAT IS NOT CONTESTED, because the brain and section 5 settled it: a printer that needs somebody is a row in Needs a look in its own words; found printers arrive as one line in the band and a dot on the + door, never a screen; Add is not a tab; and the wall never starts a print or heats anything -- that is done at the printer. The adding boards are on their own page and work with any of the three.

A PRINTER IS NOT A LAMP. It is the first thing in the house that is on for a known length of time and then finishes, that has a camera of its own, and that can need a person halfway through. A lamp is on until somebody turns it off. That difference is the whole argument between A and B.

TODAY -- THE ROOMS TAB, AND THE GARAGE WITH THREE PRINTERS IN IT

Drawn from the shipped panel on the mock house at 1440 x 900 -- the Wall layout with the tabs across the top, in Plus Jakarta, on the glass face: the bar with its three tabs and its two round buttons, the house line, and the ranked bento, every card at the size and place rooms.ts gives it.

The note over the corner is what is really in the garage. GET /printers has answered with all of it since the brain learned printers; nothing in app/src asks. And the + door has no dot, though the hub has found three printers on the Wi-Fi: TopBar.vue counts store.found and the strip, and printers are neither.

A -- IN ITS ROOM

A printer is a thing in the garage, beside the blind and the camera. Printing is a way of being on: the tile carries the printer's camera across its top, how far, and when it will be done. A stopped printer's tile turns the fault color and says the printer's own sentence, with its Help. A ready one is a plain small tile. One tap back, on Rooms, the garage card climbs the ranking because something in it is on, and wears the camera behind its name the way a filming room does.

FOR: nothing new to learn. A printer is reached the way everything else in the house is reached, and every printer has a home whether it is printing or not -- Vega, ready and idle, is still somewhere you can point at.

AGAINST: a room is a question the hub cannot answer. The brain gives a printer no room, so adding one would have to ask "Where is Atlas?" -- a second question in a flow that today needs only a tap at the printer. And it files a print two taps from where anybody is standing: Atlas finishing at 4:20 PM is news, and A puts it under Garage. Your afternoon would show it only the way it shows any device that is on, ranked among lamps, with no notion that it ends.

B -- NOW: A PRINT LEADS YOUR AFTERNOON

While there is a print, it is the first card in the row, the way a show that is playing leads it: the camera across the top, the part's picture and name, how far, and when it will be done. The rest of the house moves along one card. There are no buttons on it while it prints -- a sleeve against a kitchen wall must not pause a three-hour print -- and one tap opens the printer's pane.

A CARD FOR EVERY PRINT, NOT FOR EVERY PRINTER. When Atlas is Ready again the card goes, at a moment nobody is watching (the done map in store.ts, swept by App.vue). Juno, stopped with nothing on its bed, is not a card: it is a job, so it is the band's line and a row on Needs a look, which the brain already sends.

FOR: it puts the one thing in the house with an end time where the household already looks, and it costs no question when a printer is added -- the brain needs no room. It is the media card's argument, already won once.

AGAINST: an idle printer has no place on the three tabs. Vega, ready, is only under This house, Printers (drawn on the adding page). That is honest -- there is nothing a wall may do to an idle printer -- but somebody looking for it on Rooms will not find it.

ANSWERED 2 OCTOBER, BY AN OPTIONAL ROOM. A household that wants a printer on Rooms chooses a room for it on its pane, and it is A's tile there too (RoomChoiceB, WorkshopB, RankedB). THIS CARD IS UNCHANGED EITHER WAY: a print leads Your afternoon whether or not its printer has a room.

C -- WATCHED: PRINTERS ARE WHERE THE CAMERAS ARE

A printer is the camera on it, on the Cameras tab, with its words and its progress laid over the frame: Atlas at 42% with the bar along the frame's foot, Juno in the fault color saying it stopped, Vega live and ready. The house's own cameras follow. Opening one is the shipped camera viewer, with the printer's progress, temperatures and two actions over its foot.

FOR: what people do with a printer they are not standing at is look at it -- a lifted corner, a tangle, a part that is done. C gives the camera the most room of the three, it fills a tab that is sparse in most houses, and it needs no room either.

AGAINST: a printer is not a camera, and the tab's name stops being true. A printer without a camera has nowhere to go. And Cameras is a tab somebody opens on purpose: Atlas finishing, or waiting for a spool, is said only by the band, so C is quiet about the moment that matters most. It is the best place to watch a print and the worst place to hear about one.

B ON A PHONE

The Stack home a phone gets, as it ships, with the print under the band and above what is on: "Printing" as a short block of its own, the camera on the left, how far and when on the right. One tap opens the pane as a sheet -- the camera across the top, the same words, the same temperatures, the same two actions, and the hub's limit said once at the foot.

The phone is where B pays off most. On the wall a print is one card among several; on a phone it is often the reason the app was opened.

TODAY -- YOUR AFTERNOON

The Wall home as it ships: the weather large on the left and what is on beside it, a row you sweep. The band carries the one printer that gets through, and it is the broken one. Once the brain's notes() ships, Juno is filed in Needs a look in its own words -- and the row it opens offers Open, to a printer the panel has no screen for. That half-wired row ships with the brain whichever direction is chosen, which is why the pane should be built first.

And Atlas, an hour and fifty minutes into a three-and-a-half-hour print, is not here at all.

WHAT OPENS -- THE SAME PANE FOR A AND B

The device pane at the shipped .opened-panel geometry (0, 225; the words in a 560-wide column at 49): what it is, its name, what it is doing, how far as the largest thing on the screen, the bar with the layer and the time left, and the three temperatures. In A its first line names the room instead of "3D printer".

TEMPERATURES STAY IN CELSIUS, WITH THE C WRITTEN. The house reads in Fahrenheit, but a nozzle at 428 degrees means nothing to anybody who prints; the printer's own screen, its slicer and every spool label say 220. The C makes the exception visible rather than silent.

THE TWO THINGS A WALL MAY DO TO A PRINT are the printer's own actions, as it offers them -- here Pause and Stop print. Stop asks twice, the way removing a thing does on Needs a look, because a stopped print cannot be resumed. The right side is the camera, large, and what is being printed, with its picture and its color. "Starting a print, and saying the bed is clear, happen at Atlas" says the hub's limit once, plainly, where somebody would look for a Start button.

B -- THE CARD IN EACH STATE

The same card at its real size, in the states a printer reports, with when each arrives and when it goes. Printing has no buttons. Waiting for you is the only state with buttons on the card, because the question is the reason the card is there -- and its two answers are the printer's own (swap_slot and resume), in its own words. Done is drained rather than gone, per section 4: it says when it finished and holds its place until Atlas is Ready again. A printer that stopped with nothing printing is not a card.

ONE RULE THIS NEEDS, pinned by a test like rooms.test.ts: the band does not repeat what a card on the same screen already says. Atlas waiting for you would otherwise be the card and a Needs a look line above it, the same sentence twice.

WHAT OPENS, IN C -- THE CAMERA VIEWER

The viewer the doorbell opens today (80, 90, 1280 x 720), with the printer's progress, temperatures and two actions laid over its foot and a progress bar along its bottom edge. It is the best view of a print in any of the three, and it is a view: the words are smaller, and the temperatures are chips on a picture rather than readings you can find again in the same place.

CHOSEN 2 OCTOBER 2026 -- B, WITH AN OPTIONAL ROOM

Jordan picked B, and asked what happens when somebody wants their printers in a room -- an office, a workshop. The answer is B plus an optional room: A's tile, only where a room is chosen.

A print leads Your afternoon, where people look, whether or not its printer has a room. The room is the household's choice and never a setup question: adding a printer never asks for one, and a new printer lives under This house, Printers. A room is chosen later from the printer's own pane, with the picker every light already uses (RoomChoiceB). A printer with a room is A's tile in that room (WorkshopB), and printing counts as on for the ranking (RankedB). A's In its room board and C's Watched board stay on this page as the record of why.

RECOMMENDATION -- B, WITH AN OPTIONAL ROOM (A'S TILE, ONLY WHERE A ROOM IS CHOSEN)

B, because a print is an event with an end and the panel already knows how to show one: the show that is playing leads the row. "Done at 4:20 PM" sits where the household already looks, attention stays where section 5 put it -- the band and Needs a look for a printer with nothing printing, the card itself for a print that needs somebody -- and the card is the same whether or not the printer has a room.

THE ROOM IS THE HOUSEHOLD'S CHOICE, NEVER A SETUP QUESTION. Adding stays one tap at the printer; nothing asks "Where is Atlas?". A household that wants its printers in the workshop says so on the printer's pane, and from then on A's tile is there too, as a second place to find it, never instead of the first.

THE PANE FIRST. It is what the half-wired Open on Needs a look needs the day the brain ships, and it is where the room is chosen.

The first draft of this note recommended B alone, with A's tile as a possible later addition. Jordan's question made it now.

OR SOMETHING ELSE -- I'LL DESCRIBE IT. A real option, as ever.

B, A ROOM IF YOU WANT ONE -- THE PANE'S OWN PICKER

The pane's room line is where every pane has it, above the name. A printer starts with none, so it reads "No room - Choose", in the quiet dashed word the pane already uses for "Show this as". Choose does what the pane's Rename or move it does for a light (Opened.vue's edit head): the room line and the name become the room picker and a name field, with Done and Cancel. Drawn open, the list is the house's rooms -- Living Room, Kitchen, Bedroom, Robin's room, Theater, Garage, Outside -- and A new room..., the sort page's way of making one.

ONE ADDITION to the picker: No room, at the top. A light always has a room; a printer is allowed not to, and has to be able to go back to having none. That is the only new thing here.

B, WITH A ROOM CHOSEN -- THE WORKSHOP

A room made with A new room, holding Atlas printing and Vega ready as A's tiles, among the room's own things: the bench light, the air filter, the door. The room's line says it the way it says a light ("Atlas printing - Vega ready - Bench light on"), and the head carries each printer as a chip. Juno has no room and lives only under This house, Printers; a stopped printer in a room would be A's fault tile there, and still Needs a look's row.

AND YOUR AFTERNOON IS UNCHANGED. The print card leads it whether or not Atlas has a room -- the room adds a second place to find the printer; it never moves the first.

B, WITH A ROOM CHOSEN -- ON ROOMS

The house's rooms, ranked the way rooms.ts ranks them. Printing counts as on, so while Atlas prints the Workshop ranks among the lit rooms -- second here, behind the room with the television on -- with the printer's camera behind its name the way a filming room shows its camera, and the time left and the bar on its foot. When the print is done and nothing else in the Workshop is on, it falls back to the quiet end with the other rooms. A printer that is ready, like Vega, does not count as on.

LETTING A PRINTER IN -- THE QUESTION

The knock decision (22 September, design/knock/, C with A) already says how anything new arrives: one line in the band and a dot on the + door, and the page fills only when somebody is already on Add. Printers follow it exactly, and nothing here reopens it.

What these boards decide is the part only a printer has: the hub does not let itself in. It asks; the printer shows "Maple Court hub wants to connect" on its own screen; somebody standing at it taps Allow -- or a phone that already has that printer, at home. An ask lasts two minutes.

So Add has to say, while it waits, exactly where the yes happens and on which printer, and it has to answer all four ways the wait ends: allowed, said no, nobody answered, and could not reach. These boards work with A, B or C; they are drawn with B's Your afternoon behind them.

1 -- FOUND, AS A LINE AND A DOT

"Found 3 new things nearby", with their names under it -- word for word the line a Hue bridge gets. The way to get there is to add found printers to the house's list of things waiting (store.found, or a second source waitingBand() reads), so the count in the + door's label, the dot and the one-hour fold come free and stay pinned by adding.test.ts. The line says they are 3D printers, because a name like Juno explains nothing to somebody who did not set it up.

They are found by asking the relay which printers share the house's connection (nearby.elyir.app) and then asking each one whether it is a printer; opening Add asks again at once (POST /printers/look), which is the Look half of the knock decision.

2 -- ADD, OPEN

The shipped Add page, unchanged above the fold, with a section of its own: "Printers on this Wi-Fi", one row each and one button. It is separate from "Already waiting" because a printer is added differently -- the tap asks the printer, and the next step happens somewhere else -- and a household should know that before it taps, not after.

3 -- ASKED: THE ROW BECOMES THE INSTRUCTION

The row grows in place into what to do, named for the printer: "Tap Allow on Atlas's screen". Beside it is the printer's own screen as it looks at that moment, so the wall says where to look by showing it. Under it, the other way to say yes, and how long the ask has left (two minutes at the printer; ASK_FOR in printers.py waits a little longer). Stop asking is there because somebody who walked to the wrong printer should not have to wait out the clock.

THE INSET IS THE PRINTER'S OWN CARD, COPIED, NOT WRITTEN. Astromech's AskCard.vue (origin/main), drawn at its 800 x 480 design size and scaled: "Maple Court hub wants to connect", "A home hub on this Wi-Fi - asks for 1:42 more", its paragraph, and Allow and Not now in its own order and colors. One thing to take back to that card: its paragraph says the asker "could ... start prints when it's at home", which is the phone's sentence; a hub never starts prints, so a hub's ask wants its own line there.

4 -- THE ANSWERS, IN THE ROW THAT ASKED

Allowed: the row turns the live color, says Atlas is in the house and what it is doing, and offers Open. Refused: "Juno said no", with Ask again. Expired: "Nobody answered on Vega", with how long an ask lasts. Failed: "Couldn't reach Vega", with the one thing to check. Every row keeps its place, saying what it now is, per section 4; the answered ones leave when Add is closed.

And This house gains Printers, on the left: every printer in the house, printing or not, where one is forgotten (DELETE /printers/{id} also takes the hub off the printer's own list). Under B it is where an idle printer lives.
